question: What was the Congress leaders' approach to achieving limited self-government in the early years? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (11/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Peaceful petitions
Violent protests
Foreign intervention
Revolutionary wars
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Peaceful petitions

Explanation:
In the early years (1885-1905), the Congress leaders' approach to achieving limited self-government was based on peaceful petitions. They were loyal to British rule and sought reforms through constitutional means. Leaders believed that through petitions, representation, and the press, they could influence the British government. This phase is known as the Moderate Phase. The Indian Councils Act of 1892 increased limited Indian representation in legislative councils. Leaders like Dadabhai Naoroji and Gopal Krishna Gokhale demanded self-government through peaceful methods. Later, the Swadeshi Movement of 1905 adopted a more assertive approach.

question_hi: कांग्रेस नेताओं का शुरुआती वर्षों में सीमित स्व-शासन प्राप्त करने का दृष्टिकोण क्या था? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (11/08/2025) Shift 2)
options_hi: शांतिपूर्ण याचिकाएं
हिंसक विरोध
विदेशी हस्तक्षेप
क्रांतिकारी युद्ध
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है शांतिपूर्ण याचिकाएं

Explanation:
कांग्रेस के शुरुआती वर्षों (1885-1905) में नेताओं का दृष्टिकोण शांतिपूर्ण याचिकाओं पर आधारित था। वे ब्रिटिश शासन के प्रति वफादार थे और संवैधानिक तरीकों से सुधार चाहते थे। नेताओं का मानना था कि याचिकाएं, प्रतिनिधित्व और प्रेस के माध्यम से ब्रिटिश सरकार को प्रभावित किया जा सकता है। इस चरण को उदारवादी चरण कहा जाता है। 1892 के भारतीय परिषद अधिनियम ने विधान परिषदों में सीमित भारतीय प्रतिनिधित्व बढ़ाया। दादाभाई नौरोजी और गोपाल कृष्ण गोखले जैसे नेताओं ने शांतिपूर्ण तरीकों से स्वशासन की मांग की। बाद में 1905 के स्वदेशी आंदोलन ने अधिक मुखर दृष्टिकोण अपनाया।

question: Who among the following was arrested and imprisoned for refusing to give evidence against Aurobindo Ghosh in the Bande Mataram conspiracy case? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (11/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Garimella Satyanarayana
Kanaiyalal Maneklal Munshi
Bipin Chandra Pal
Peer Ali Khan
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Bipin Chandra Pal

Explanation:
Bipin Chandra Pal was a prominent Indian nationalist leader. During the 1907-1908 'Bande Mataram' conspiracy case against Aurobindo Ghosh for sedition, the government pressured Pal to testify against Aurobindo. Pal refused, leading to his arrest and imprisonment. This act signified moral courage in India's freedom struggle. Pal was a member of the 'Lal-Bal-Pal' trio and a strong advocate of the Swadeshi movement. His refusal to give false evidence highlighted his integrity and commitment to the nationalist cause.

question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से किसे वंदे मातरम षडयंत्र मामले में अरबिंदो घोष के खिलाफ गवाही देने से इनकार करने पर गिरफ्तार और कैद किया गया था? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (11/08/2025) Shift 3)

पीर अली खान
solution_hi:

Explanation:
बिपिन चंद्र पाल एक प्रमुख भारतीय राष्ट्रवादी नेता थे। 1907-1908 में 'वंदे मातरम' षडयंत्र मामले में अरबिंदो घोष पर राजद्रोह का मुकदमा चला था। सरकार ने पाल को अरबिंदो के खिलाफ गवाही देने के लिए दबाव डाला, लेकिन उन्होंने इनकार कर दिया। इस कारण उन्हें गिरफ्तार कर कैद कर लिया गया। यह घटना भारतीय स्वतंत्रता संग्राम में नैतिक साहस का प्रतीक है। बिपिन चंद्र पाल 'लाल-बाल-पाल' त्रिमूर्ति के सदस्य थे और स्वदेशी आंदोलन के प्रबल समर्थक थे।

question: The Devi Movement took place in which of the following regions of India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (11/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Western Maharashtra
North Gujarat
South Gujarat
Eastern Madhya Pradesh
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is South Gujarat

Explanation:
The Devi Movement took place in the South Gujarat region of India. It was a socio-religious movement launched by the tribal community in 1922-23. The movement was led by Motilal Tejawat. Its objective was to keep tribals away from alcohol and superstition. The movement also supported Gandhian ideology. The Devi Movement is also known as the Bhagat Movement.

Explanation:

question: Which of the following was the objective of the law enacted in 1856 in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (12/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Banning of child labour
Abolition of caste system
Temple entry for Shudras
Legalising widow remarriage
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Legalising widow remarriage

Explanation:
The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act (Act XV of 1856) enacted in 1856 legalised the remarriage of Hindu widows. This act was drafted during the tenure of Lord Dalhousie but was passed under Lord Canning. The efforts of Raja Ram Mohan Roy and the campaign led by Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar played a crucial role in the enactment of this law. It aimed to eradicate the social evil of enforced widowhood and provided widows with the opportunity to reintegrate into society. This was a landmark step in the social reform movement in India.

question: Who was called the 'Grand Old Man of India' and the first Indian to demand Swaraj? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (12/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Surendranath Banerjee
Gopal Krishna Gokhale
Bal Gangadhar Tilak
Dadabhai Naoroji
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Dadabhai Naoroji

Explanation:
Dadabhai Naoroji was called the 'Grand Old Man of India'. He was the first Indian to demand 'Swaraj' (self-rule) at the 1906 Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress. Naoroji was a renowned economist, educator, and politician. He was also the first Indian to be elected to the British Parliament. His famous book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' highlighted the economic drain of India under British rule.

question: Which of the following best defines the strategy of Passive Resistance as advocated by Extremists? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (12/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Boycott, Swadeshi and non-cooperation with rulers
Assassination of British officers
Military training of Indian youth abroad
Armed confrontation with colonial forces
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Boycott, Swadeshi and non-cooperation with rulers

Explanation:
Extremists advocated a strategy of passive resistance, which meant opposing British rule without violence. It included Boycott (of foreign goods and institutions), Swadeshi (promotion of indigenous products), and Non-cooperation (renunciation of government offices and honors). This strategy was promoted by leaders like Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Lala Lajpat Rai. Its aim was to create economic and political pressure, not armed rebellion. Extremists believed that mass participation could achieve freedom.

☛ Methods of passive resistance → Boycott, Swadeshi, Non-cooperation
☛ Objective of Swadeshi movement → Boycott foreign goods and promote indigenous industries
☛ Target of Boycott → British goods and institutions
☛ Meaning of Non-cooperation → Renunciation of government jobs, titles, and honors
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा चरमपंथियों द्वारा वकालत की गई निष्क्रिय प्रतिरोध की रणनीति को सर्वोत्तम रूप से परिभाषित करता है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (12/08/2025) Shift 2)

solution_hi:

Explanation:

question: Which of the following British officials found India as an uncivilised country and had to be civilised, following which the English Education Act of 1835 was introduced?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (13/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Henry Thomas Colebrooke
William Jones
Thomas Macaulay
Nathaniel Halhed
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Thomas Macaulay

Explanation:
Thomas Babington Macaulay sharply criticized Indian culture and civilization, calling India an 'uncivilised' country. His efforts led to the English Education Act of 1835, which established Western education in India. Macaulay's objective was to create 'a class who may be interpreters between us and the millions whom we govern—a class of persons Indian in blood and colour, but English in taste, in opinions, in morals, and in intellect.' The Act made English the medium of instruction and neglected oriental education. Macaulay's Minute (1835) laid the foundation of Indian education policy. This act was passed under Governor-General Lord William Bentinck and significantly shaped the British education system in India.

question: Who among the following had given the idea to mobilise all the leading Indian political leaders under a common platform called the Indian National Congress? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (13/08/2025) Shift 2)

Explanation:
The idea of forming the Indian National Congress was given by Allan Octavian Hume, a retired British civil servant. He believed that a common platform was needed to bring together leading Indian political leaders to voice their grievances and seek reforms. The first session of the Congress was held in Pune (Bombay) in 1885 under the presidency of W.C. Bannerjee. Hume's initiative was supported by prominent Indian leaders like Dadabhai Naoroji and Surendranath Banerjee. The Congress initially aimed at promoting dialogue between Indians and the British government, focusing on administrative and political reforms. Although leaders like Surendranath Banerjee and Ananda Mohan Bose were influential, the original concept of the Congress was Hume's.

question: Who among the following was the first political leader in India to openly put forward, in his newspaper Bande Mataram, the idea of complete independence for the country? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (13/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Swami Vivekananda

solution:

Explanation:
Sri Aurobindo was the first political leader in India to openly advocate for complete independence (Purna Swaraj) through his newspaper Bande Mataram. In the year 1907, he published articles demanding full political freedom from British rule. Before this, most leaders were demanding Home Rule or colonial reforms. Sri Aurobindo gave a new direction to nationalist ideology and inspired the youth. His newspaper Bande Mataram became a major medium for revolutionary ideas. Later, Mahatma Gandhi advocated for complete independence in the 1920s, but Sri Aurobindo was the first to put forward this idea openly.

question: The Dutch East India Company established its first factory in India in _________.  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (13/08/2025) Shift 3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a major cause of the people’s revolts before 1857? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (14/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Exploitation of rural society by corrupt officers.
Destruction of indigenous industries.
Conversion of people to Christianity.
Colonial land revenue settlements.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Conversion of people to Christianity

Explanation:
Major causes of the people's revolts before 1857 included socio-economic discontent arising from colonial policies. Exploitation of rural society by corrupt officers, destruction of indigenous industries, and colonial land revenue settlements (e.g., Permanent Settlement, Ryotwari) led to heavy taxation and land alienation for peasants and artisans. While conversion programs were part of missionary activities and became a spark for the 1857 revolt, it was not a major cause in earlier revolts (e.g., Santhal, Chuar, Polygar) which were primarily against economic and administrative oppression rather than religious issues. These uprisings were rooted in grievances over revenue, land rights, and social exploitation.

question: In which year were the Indian Civil Service (ICS) and Indian Police (IP) replaced by the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) and Indian Police Service (IPS), later recognised as All-India Services? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (18/08/2025) Shift 1)

solution:

Explanation:
During the First War of Independence in 1857, the rebels declared the Mughal Emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar as their leader. He led the rebellion, but the British army recaptured Delhi. He was arrested and exiled to Rangoon (Yangon), where he died in 1862. His leadership gave the rebellion a national character.

solution_hi:

Explanation:
1857 के प्रथम स्वतंत्रता संग्राम में, विद्रोहियों ने मुगल सम्राट बहादुर शाह ज़फ़र को अपना नेता घोषित किया। दिल्ली पर कब्ज़ा करने के बाद, विद्रोहियों ने उन्हें सम्राट मान लिया और उनके नाम से फरमान जारी किए गए। बहादुर शाह ज़फ़र मुगल वंश के अंतिम सम्राट थे। उन्होंने विद्रोह का नेतृत्व किया, लेकिन ब्रिटिश सेना ने दिल्ली पर पुनः कब्जा कर लिया। उन्हें गिरफ्तार कर रंगून (यांगून) निर्वासित कर दिया गया, जहां 1862 में उनकी मृत्यु हुई। उनके नेतृत्व ने विद्रोह को एक राष्ट्रीय रूप दिया।
